description: A math-oriented student who excelled in a Python-based Intro to CS course and is now transitioning to C++ with an interest in the theoretical foundations of algorithms.

nodes.personalizationRationale: As the student has no prior exposure to C++, this node provides the necessary syntax bridge from their previous general programming experience.
nodes.description: An introduction to C++ syntax, variable types, and control structures designed for students moving from Python or Java.
nodes.title: C++ Syntax for Python/Java Programmers
Pointers and Reference Mechanics
nodes.description: A deep dive into memory addresses, pointer declaration, and the difference between pass-by-value and pass-by-reference.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Pointers represent a significant hurdle for students with no prior exposure to C++, necessitating dedicated scaffolding before moving to data structure implementation.

nodes.title: Dynamic Memory and Object Lifecycle
nodes.personalizationRationale: Since the student has no prior exposure to manual memory management, this scaffolding node is critical for preventing memory leaks in later assignments.
nodes.description: Practical guide to using 'new' and 'delete' for dynamic memory and understanding the C++ object lifecycle.

nodes.personalizationRationale: This core node ensures the student masters the fundamental OOD principles required for all subsequent data structure implementations.
nodes.description: Core principles of Object-Oriented Design in C++, including classes, inheritance, and the use of templates for generic programming.
nodes.title: Classes, Inheritance, and Templates

nodes.personalizationRationale: Implementing linked lists is a mandatory skill that applies the pointer knowledge gained in the foundational block.
nodes.description: Implementation of singly and doubly linked lists, focusing on node manipulation and pointer updates.
nodes.title: Linked List Implementations

nodes.description: Assessment covering recursion principles and the application of Big-O notation to analyze algorithm efficiency.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Quiz 1 is a required checkpoint to verify the student's grasp of recursion and asymptotic analysis.
nodes.title: Quiz 1: Recursion & Big-O Analysis
Stacks and Queues ADTs
nodes.description: Defining Stack and Queue Abstract Data Types and implementing them using both arrays and linked lists.
nodes.personalizationRationale: These are fundamental sequence-based structures that every student must master for the midterm.

nodes.title: Vectors and Iterator Patterns
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core understanding of vectors and iterators is essential for professional C++ development and course success.
nodes.description: Exploring the STL vector class and the design pattern of iterators for traversing sequence containers.

nodes.title: Sequences and Bubble Sort
nodes.personalizationRationale: Bubble sort serves as a core introductory algorithm for understanding sequence-based complexity.
nodes.description: Analysis of sequence-based sorting using Bubble Sort and the logic behind sequence manipulation.

nodes.title: Midterm Review Checkpoint
nodes.personalizationRationale: A mandatory review node to ensure the student is prepared for the high-stakes midterm exam.
nodes.description: Comprehensive review of material from blocks 1 through 3 in preparation for the midterm examination.
Introduction to general tree structures, terminology, and depth-first vs. breadth-first traversal algorithms.
nodes.personalizationRationale: General trees are a required topic for understanding hierarchical data organization.
nodes.title: General Trees and Traversals

nodes.personalizationRationale: Binary trees form the basis for more complex search structures covered later in the course.
nodes.description: Specialized study of binary trees, their properties, and recursive implementation of traversals.
nodes.title: Binary Tree Properties and Implementation

nodes.description: Implementation of priority queues using binary heaps and understanding the heap-order property.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Heaps are a core requirement for efficient data selection and sorting applications.
nodes.title: Heaps and Priority Queues

nodes.personalizationRationale: Mastery of hash tables is a core objective for achieving constant-time data retrieval.
nodes.description: Design of hash functions and strategies for collision resolution in hash tables.
nodes.title: Hash Tables and Map ADTs

nodes.personalizationRationale: BSTs are foundational search structures that every student is examined on.
nodes.description: Construction and operation of Binary Search Trees (BST) and the necessity of self-balancing.
nodes.title: Binary Search Trees (BST)
AVL and Red-Black Trees
nodes.description: Advanced study of AVL trees and Red-Black trees to maintain logarithmic search times.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Self-balancing trees represent the most complex theory-heavy core material in the syllabus.
These sorting algorithms are required capstone knowledge for the final cumulative exam.
nodes.description: Detailed comparison of Merge Sort and Selection Sort, focusing on time and space complexity.
nodes.title: Merge Sort and Selection Sort Analysis
Cumulative Final Exam Review
nodes.personalizationRationale: The mandatory final review ensures all cumulative learning objectives are met before the final exam.
nodes.description: Cumulative review of all course topics and final assessment of data structure design proficiency.
